items.name: B2B SaaS
items.pattern: Hero with one claim + logo wall + 3-up problem/solution + product screenshot + features + integrations + pricing table + FAQ + closing CTA
items.colorMood: Trust blue carrying every surface, the teal accent spent only on the primary CTA and nothing else
items.typeMood: Professional, strong hierarchy, nothing decorative — the screenshot is the hero, type is the frame
effects: subtle hover lift 200ms ease-out
logo wall greyscale until hover
sticky nav that gains a border on scroll, not a shadow
numbers count up once on first view, never again

decisionRules.if: pre-launch / no product yet
decisionRules.then: waitlist pattern — one email field, no pricing table, no fake testimonials, no logo wall of companies you do not have

decisionRules.if: the product is data-heavy (tables, grids, reports)
decisionRules.then: drop bento-grid inside the app — bento is a marketing device; a grid of unequal cards is the wrong shape for rows of like items

decisionRules.if: enterprise deal size (>$25k ACV)
decisionRules.then: replace the pricing table with 'Talk to sales' + a security/compliance section — a price tag invites procurement to anchor against it

decisionRules.if: self-serve PLG motion
decisionRules.then: the CTA is 'Start free', never 'Request demo' — a demo form is a churn valve on a credit-card funnel

antiPatterns: Dark mode by default — buyers evaluate on a projector in a lit room
Stock-photo hero of people pointing at a laptop
Carousel of testimonials nobody reads and nobody can Ctrl+F
A pricing table with four tiers where two are decoys
'Trusted by' logos at 40% opacity that turn out to be free-tier signups

pages.dashboard: Sidebar nav + KPI row + one primary table. Density over whitespace — the daily user wants rows, not air.
pages.pricing: Three tiers max, most-popular marked once, annual/monthly toggle, feature matrix below the fold. Every row in the matrix must be a real differentiator.
pages.login: Single column, 400px, logo + email + SSO. No marketing copy, no hero image, no nav.

items.name: Micro-SaaS
items.pattern: Hero with the exact job-to-be-done in one line + a 20-second demo GIF + three features + one price + founder note with a real face + CTA
items.colorMood: Sherbet backgrounds doing the personality work while every foreground stays dark enough to read — candy surfaces, grown-up text
items.typeMood: Opinionated and fast — a product that has taste and no design committee
effects: hard 4px offset shadow that collapses to 0 on press
thick black outline on every interactive element
demo GIF autoplays muted, loops, no controls
no scroll animation anywhere — the page is 900px tall

decisionRules.if: one founder with no designer
decisionRules.then: neo-brutalism is the correct hedge — its rules are mechanical (border 3px, shadow 4px/4px, radius 0) so they survive being applied by someone who is not a designer; swiss-minimal in the same hands collapses on the first 13px margin

decisionRules.if: the product touches money, health or legal data
decisionRules.then: abandon neo-brutalism entirely — the toy vocabulary reads as a hobby project and your conversion problem becomes a trust problem

decisionRules.if: traffic comes from Product Hunt / HN / X
decisionRules.then: the hero must state the job in the first 8 words — this audience bounces in 3 seconds and never scrolls

decisionRules.if: pricing is under $20/mo
decisionRules.then: one price, one button, no tiers — a comparison table on a $9 product costs more attention than the decision is worth

antiPatterns: Cosplaying enterprise — a 'Trusted by' wall and an SSO badge on a two-week-old product
An 'Enterprise: Contact us' tier that goes to a founder's personal inbox
Fake urgency countdowns on a subscription
A roadmap page that has not moved in eight months
Pastel + thin grey text — the palette's whole discipline is dark foregrounds

items.name: Fintech / Banking
items.pattern: Hero with the balance/number as the hero + regulator and insurance badges + how-it-works in three steps + security section + fee transparency table + FAQ + CTA
items.colorMood: Deep green over graphite — serious rather than startup-cheerful; amber accent reserved for pending states, never for decoration
items.typeMood: Institutional, audited, calm — tabular figures everywhere a number can change
effects: tabular-nums on every currency figure so digits do not jitter as they update
no animation on a balance — a number that slides looks like a number that is unsure
row hover as a 1px background shift, nothing more
state changes announced to screen readers, not just colored

decisionRules.if: regulated disclosure (APR, fees, risk warnings, FSCS/FDIC status)
decisionRules.then: the disclosure cannot be behind a tooltip, an accordion or a hover — it renders at the point of decision, at body size, in foreground color. A tooltip is not disclosure; it is a defence you will lose

decisionRules.if: consumer mobile banking rather than a back-office console
decisionRules.then: drop data-dense entirely — it assumes 1440px and a mouse. One balance per screen, 44px targets, the primary action reachable by thumb

decisionRules.if: the number on screen is money the user can lose
decisionRules.then: destructive and confirm are different colors AND different words — 'Send £4,200 to Jane Doe' on the button, never 'Confirm'

decisionRules.if: the product shows gains/losses
decisionRules.then: never encode direction in red/green alone — 8% of male users cannot separate them; ship arrow + sign + color together

antiPatterns: Gradient hero on a bank — it reads as a crypto scam to the exact demographic with money
Hiding fees in a modal the user must open to find
Red/green as the only signal for up/down
Animated counters on a live balance
A dark-pattern 'skip for now' that is styled more prominently than the security step

pages.dashboard: Balance first and largest, then this month's flow, then the transaction table. Density over whitespace — this is a daily expert screen.
pages.checkout: One column, amount restated at every step, no upsells between the user and the confirm button.
pages.onboarding: KYC in named steps with a visible position indicator. Never ask for a document without saying why you need it and who sees it.

items.name: Crypto / Web3
items.pattern: Hero with the protocol claim + live TVL/volume stats bar + connect-wallet CTA + how-it-works + audit and contract links + docs link + community CTA
items.colorMood: Bullion on carbon — gold carries the weight, the violet spark is one accent; deliberately not neon toy energy
items.typeMood: Monospace as a credibility signal — addresses, hashes and amounts must align vertically or they cannot be compared
effects: addresses always truncated middle (0x1a2b…9f0e) with click-to-copy and a copied confirmation
live stats tick without layout shift — reserve the width for the widest value
glow on the CTA edge only, never under text
pending transaction state persists across a refresh

decisionRules.if: the screen is an order book, portfolio or position table
decisionRules.then: data-dense wins and the glow dies — cyberpunk's own rule is that it fails on large data tables; every glowing edge competes for the attention a price change needs

decisionRules.if: the action is irreversible (send, swap, approve, sign)
decisionRules.then: show the resolved human meaning, not the payload — 'You are granting unlimited USDC spend to 0x1a2b…' beats a hex blob every time. Unlimited approvals need a second, deliberate step

decisionRules.if: targeting non-degen / first-time users
decisionRules.then: cut the neon and the jargon — 'gas', 'slippage' and 'bridge' are the top-3 drop-off words; explain in the UI or lose them at the first modal

decisionRules.if: the product is a wallet
decisionRules.then: seed-phrase screens get no analytics, no screenshots, no clipboard auto-clear surprises, and no dark surface that hides a shoulder-surfer's reflection

antiPatterns: Neon everything until an actual price is unreadable
A raw hex payload as the confirmation screen
TVL counters that animate on every render
'Audited' with no link to the report or the auditor
Connect-wallet as the first thing on the page, before the product has been explained

items.name: Healthcare
items.pattern: Hero with a calm human claim + find-care / book-appointment entry + conditions or services + your-care-team + insurance and cost clarity + accessibility statement + contact with a real phone number
items.colorMood: Teal and cool white that reads as competent care rather than emergency — red exists only for genuine clinical alarm
items.typeMood: Clinical without being cold — 18px floor, generous line height, a person's voice not a form's
effects: no motion on anything clinical — vestibular disorders are a patient population, not an edge case
focus rings that survive a high-contrast OS mode
loading states say what is loading ('Fetching your results…')
error text is adjacent to the field, in words, never a red border alone

decisionRules.if: the user is reading this while anxious or in pain (results, diagnosis, ER wayfinding)
decisionRules.then: one decision per screen, plain language at grade-8, and the next action stated as a verb — cognitive load is a symptom here, not a preference

decisionRules.if: a dose, frequency or interaction is on screen
decisionRules.then: it renders at body size in foreground color with units spelled out — never abbreviated, never in a tooltip, never grey. 'Sketch', 'draft' or playful styling next to a dose is a safety defect

decisionRules.if: the audience skews 65+
decisionRules.then: 18px is the floor not the ceiling, targets 48px, and never rely on a hover state — a shaky hand and a trackpad do not produce reliable hovers

decisionRules.if: PHI is displayed
decisionRules.then: no PHI in URLs, no PHI in analytics payloads, and an obvious, always-reachable sign-out — shared clinic machines are the default deployment, not the exception

antiPatterns: Neumorphism or any low-contrast aesthetic — low contrast IS the style, and you cannot fix it and keep it
Stock photo of a smiling doctor with folded arms and a stethoscope
Symptom checkers styled as a fun quiz
Cost 'from £X' with the real number three clicks away
A chatbot as the only route to a human when the user is describing chest pain

pages.dashboard: Next appointment first, then results needing attention, then messages. Nothing else competes.
pages.onboarding: Intake in short named steps, progress visible, every field justified. Allow save-and-return — patients fill these in from waiting rooms.

items.name: E-commerce
items.pattern: Hero shot + category tiles + best-sellers grid + social proof + shipping/returns promise + newsletter + footer with trust marks. PDP: gallery left, buy box right, details below, related last
items.colorMood: Burnt orange makes Buy inviting rather than shouty; the green accent is reserved for 'in stock' and confirmation and is never spent elsewhere
items.typeMood: Restrained premium retail — the serif sets the brand, the sans does the selling; price is never the biggest thing on the page
effects: image zoom on hover for desktop, pinch for touch — never a lightbox that traps focus
add-to-cart confirms in place with the item, not a full-page redirect
skeleton tiles at the real aspect ratio so the grid never reflows
sticky buy box on the PDP below 1024px

decisionRules.if: the product's color, texture or fit is the purchase decision (apparel, furniture, cosmetics)
decisionRules.then: photography budget is the design budget — a stock hero is worse than a plain gradient, and swatches must be real photographs, not CSS hex circles

decisionRules.if: the market is data-conscious or on slow connections
decisionRules.then: the hero IS your LCP — one responsive AVIF/WebP under 100KB, everything else lazy; a 2MB hero is a conversion bug, not a design choice

decisionRules.if: checkout
decisionRules.then: guest checkout is not optional, the total including shipping and tax appears before the payment step, and nothing new is introduced between the user and Pay — a surprise cost at step 4 is the single largest abandonment cause

decisionRules.if: the catalog exceeds ~200 SKUs
decisionRules.then: faceted filters that persist in the URL beat any amount of art direction — and drop dark-luxury/gold hairlines, they do not survive a 200-tile grid

antiPatterns: Cart that redirects to a full page and loses the browse context
Discount modal before the visitor has seen a single product
Fake 'only 2 left' scarcity — it is now illegal in the EU and it is obvious anyway
Reviews that cannot be sorted or filtered to the 1-star
Free-shipping threshold revealed only at the payment step

pages.product: Gallery left (real photos, zoomable), buy box right and sticky, variant swatches as images, stock and delivery date stated, details and reviews below, related last.
pages.checkout: Single column, visible step count, total with shipping and tax from step 1, guest path first, payment last. No nav, no upsell, no exit.
pages.search-results: Facets in a left rail that persist in the URL, result count stated, zero-results offers a real alternative not an apology.

items.name: Luxury / Fashion
items.pattern: Full-bleed campaign image + house name only + collection index + editorial story + lookbook + stockists/boutiques + a quiet contact. Navigation is a word, not a bar
items.colorMood: Near-black, bone white and a single champagne gold with nothing else permitted to compete
items.typeMood: Cover-of-Vogue confidence — extreme contrast, acres of white space, the logotype never explains itself
effects: cross-fade between campaign images, 600ms, no easing tricks
cursor becomes a thin ring over imagery
type enters once on load, never on scroll
zero hover chrome on product tiles — the photograph is the affordance

decisionRules.if: the brand discounts or runs a sale
decisionRules.then: dark-luxury contradicts the offer at the vocabulary level — a gold hairline around 'MEGA SALE' reads as a counterfeit; move to editorial-magazine on white for that surface

decisionRules.if: the catalog exceeds ~50 SKUs
decisionRules.then: drop the gold hairlines and the 3-column air — the style does not scale past a boutique grid, it becomes an unreadable field of thin lines

decisionRules.if: the site must certify WCAG AA (EAA applies to EU retail from 2025)
decisionRules.then: the 60% grey body text that makes it look expensive is a legal failure — keep the restraint, raise the foreground to 4.5:1, spend the elegance on space instead of on low contrast

decisionRules.if: there is no photography budget
decisionRules.then: do not attempt this style — it is half imagery by weight; go typographic on white, which costs nothing and still reads as considered

antiPatterns: Light mode — the luxury signal literally was the darkness
A carousel of five hero images the visitor never sees past the first of
Thin 200-weight grey type at 14px as a substitute for actual art direction
Newsletter popup over the campaign image within 2 seconds
Any badge, ribbon, or star rating on a product tile

items.name: Restaurant / Food
items.pattern: Full-bleed dish photograph + one line of who we are + the menu (as text, on the page) + hours and address above the fold on mobile + reservation CTA + story + map
items.colorMood: Tomato on a cream tablecloth with olive — warm paper that makes you hungry rather than efficient
items.typeMood: Appetite in type — a chalkboard menu that had a very good art director; prices never in a bigger size than the dish
effects: photographs at 4:5 on mobile, 3:2 on desktop, never cropped through the plate
menu sections anchor-linked, sticky section tabs on scroll
no parallax on food — motion makes it look like a stock library
hours widget resolves 'Open now' server-side, not in the visitor's timezone

decisionRules.if: this is a local restaurant site
decisionRules.then: the four things 90% of visitors came for are hours, address, menu and phone — they go above the fold on mobile or the design has failed regardless of how it looks. A PDF menu is the single most common conversion defect in this category

decisionRules.if: food delivery / ordering rather than a restaurant site
decisionRules.then: photographic drops to thumbnail scale and speed wins — the user is hungry and choosing, not browsing art; organic-earthy cannot signal 'late' or 'cancelled', so bring in a real alert color

decisionRules.if: there is no photography budget
decisionRules.then: do not use stock food photography — it is instantly recognisable and it reads as a chain; go typographic on the menu, which is what a good bistro does anyway

decisionRules.if: allergens or dietary information exists
decisionRules.then: it is text next to the dish, not an icon key in the footer — an icon the user must decode is a liability with an anaphylaxis risk attached

antiPatterns: The menu as a PDF — unreadable on the phone that 80% of visitors are holding
Autoplay video of sizzling with sound
Hours in an image
A full-screen splash of the interior before the menu
'Book a table' that opens a third-party site with a different brand and no back button

items.name: Beauty / Spa / Wellness
items.pattern: Calm full-bleed of the space + one line of promise + treatments with duration and price + booking CTA that never leaves the page + practitioners with real faces + what to expect + location and parking
items.colorMood: Dusty rose and sage on warm plaster — quiet and skin-adjacent, where a hard edge would break the spell
items.typeMood: Quiet money — a hairline serif over a geometric sans that refuses to raise its voice
effects: cross-fades only, 800ms — nothing in this category should move quickly
no drop shadows; separation comes from warm tone shifts
booking calendar inline, never a modal that traps focus
images of the actual room, at rest, with no people in them

decisionRules.if: booking is the primary conversion
decisionRules.then: price and duration appear on the treatment card, before the calendar — a spa that hides its prices reads as expensive and untrustworthy simultaneously, and the calendar is where you lose them

decisionRules.if: medical aesthetics (injectables, laser, prescription skincare)
decisionRules.then: this is a healthcare product wearing spa clothes — the risk and aftercare disclosure cannot be behind an accordion, and 'results not typical' is not a substitute for showing typical results

decisionRules.if: the brand sells product as well as service
decisionRules.then: split the surfaces — organic-earthy cannot signal 'out of stock' or 'order failed'; bring a real alert color into the commerce path only

decisionRules.if: clients are booking on a phone between other things
decisionRules.then: the whole flow is thumb-reachable and resumable — the abandoned-booking rate in this category is a scheduling problem, not a persuasion problem

antiPatterns: Stock photo of a woman with a towel turban and cucumber slices
Prices 'on consultation' for a 30-minute manicure
Before/after galleries with different lighting, angle and makeup
Thin 200-weight blush text at 14px — the palette's discipline is dark foregrounds on soft surfaces
A booking link that opens a third-party system with a completely different visual language

items.name: Fitness / Training
items.pattern: Full-bleed athlete shot + one verb-led claim + programmes/classes + coach credibility + membership tiers + timetable + join CTA. In-app: today's session first, everything else second
items.colorMood: Volt green screaming off charcoal — high energy, and legible mid-set at arm's length
items.typeMood: Stadium volume — ultra-condensed caps that hit like a scoreboard; the rep count is the largest thing on the screen
effects: rest timer readable at arm's length — 72px minimum, no exceptions
haptic + audio on set completion, because eyes are not on the phone
no scroll animation in-app — the user is mid-set and sweaty
screen-wake lock during an active session

decisionRules.if: the screen is read mid-workout
decisionRules.then: arm's length is the design constraint — 72px numerals, 4.5:1 minimum with sweat and gym glare, and targets sized for a shaking hand. This is why high-contrast-a11y is here despite its own note about fashion-forward marketing: the marketing surface and the training surface are different products

decisionRules.if: marketing site rather than the training app
decisionRules.then: photography carries it and high-contrast steps back — but never ship a hero of a body type the product does not actually serve; the bounce is instant and it is measurable

decisionRules.if: the product tracks weight, calories or body composition
decisionRules.then: make every one of those numbers optional and never celebrate a decrease — you have eating-disorder recovery users you will never identify, and a confetti animation on a weight drop is the harm

decisionRules.if: gym check-in / kiosk context
decisionRules.then: 56px targets and high contrast — gloves, chalk, glare and a queue behind them are the design constraint

antiPatterns: Streak mechanics that punish rest days — the recovery day is the training
Thin type on the timer screen
Before/after transformation photos as the primary social proof
Class booking that requires the app when the member is standing at the door
Volt green as body text — it is a signal color, it has no business under a paragraph

items.name: Education / LMS
items.pattern: Hero with the outcome not the feature + who it is for + curriculum outline + instructor credibility + proof of completion/accreditation + price or institutional CTA + FAQ. In-app: continue-where-you-left-off first
items.colorMood: Indigo with a highlighter amber — friendly enough for a teenager, credible enough for the institution paying the invoice
items.typeMood: Legibility as the actual brief — Lexend exists because reading speed is the product here, not a preference
effects: progress is always visible and always honest — 3 of 12, never a spinner
illustration carries empty states and errors, never the content itself
autosave on every input, with a stated timestamp — students lose work on school wifi
no timed animation on an assessment screen

decisionRules.if: the buyer is a school district, university or L&D procurement
decisionRules.then: drop hand-drawn-sketch immediately — the wobble reads as unfinished to an enterprise buyer and it will be raised in the evaluation. Keep it on the student-facing surface, remove it from anything the cheque-signer sees

decisionRules.if: learners include dyslexic or ESL users (they always do)
decisionRules.then: Lexend and Atkinson Hyperlegible are load-bearing, not decorative — plus a 70-character measure, no justified text, and never encode a correct/incorrect answer in color alone

decisionRules.if: K-12 rather than adult learning
decisionRules.then: COPPA changes the design — no open comment fields, no third-party analytics on a minor, and the parent/teacher is a second user class with their own screens

decisionRules.if: the course is assessed or accredited
decisionRules.then: 'sketch' styling stops at the assessment boundary — a hand-drawn border around a graded exam reads as a draft and undermines the credential the whole product sells

antiPatterns: Gamification bolted onto content nobody finished — badges do not fix a boring module
Progress bars that count pages instead of learning
Video as the only modality, with no transcript and no text path
A 40-hour course sold with a '5 minutes a day' hero
Autoplaying to the next lesson before the learner has decided to continue

pages.dashboard: Continue where you left off, first and largest. Then due dates. Then the catalog. A student's dashboard is a resume button with decoration around it.

items.name: Kids / Family
items.pattern: Big friendly character + one enormous START button + parent gate to everything else + activity picker as large tiles + parent dashboard behind the gate
items.colorMood: Primary-colour joy with the volume up — bright blue, sunshine yellow, candy red, sized for small fingers
items.typeMood: Round, bouncy and safe for small hands — nothing here has a sharp corner
effects: every tap gets sound + squash-and-stretch + haptic — a 4-year-old needs three channels of confirmation
no timeouts, no urgency, no failure states — only 'try again' delivered by the character
targets 64px minimum, spaced 16px apart against fat-finger mis-taps
no hover states at all — this is a touch-only audience

decisionRules.if: the child is pre-reader (under ~6)
decisionRules.then: icon + color + sound + character voice must all carry the same meaning — text carries nothing. A label-only button does not exist to this user

decisionRules.if: anything costs money or leaves the app
decisionRules.then: it goes behind a real parent gate — a maths question, not a 'Are you 13?' checkbox. An IAP a child can reach with a tap is a chargeback and an app-store removal

decisionRules.if: dark mode is requested
decisionRules.then: claymorphism collapses — the light-source trick needs a bright base to read as clay at all. Ship a dimmed light theme for bedtime, not a dark theme

decisionRules.if: there is a parent-facing surface (progress, settings, billing)
decisionRules.then: it is a different product — drop claymorphism and fredoka there and use a plain adult UI; a parent evaluating a subscription in a bouncy toy interface does not trust it with a card

antiPatterns: Ads or IAP inside the child-facing surface
Streaks and loss-aversion mechanics aimed at a 5-year-old
Any collection of personal data from a minor — COPPA is not a design detail
Small text 'for the parents' inside the kids' flow
Flashing/strobing effects — photosensitive epilepsy peaks in this age group

items.name: Gaming / Esports
items.pattern: Full-bleed key art + trailer + one CTA (Wishlist/Play/Buy) + features as screenshots not bullets + system requirements + community links + storefront badges
items.colorMood: A dark room lit by a screen — magenta and cyan burning on true black; the key art supplies the rest
items.typeMood: HUD energy — clipped corners and angular terminals, a scoreboard that never sleeps
effects: trailer autoplays muted with an obvious unmute, never with sound
hover on a screenshot tile plays 3 seconds of gameplay
neon edge glow on interactive elements only — never under body text
60fps or cut the effect; a janky 3D hero on a games site is a competence signal

decisionRules.if: this is a launcher or in-game HUD rather than a marketing site
decisionRules.then: drop spatial-3d and most of the glow — nobody wants to orbit their settings page, and a HUD that competes with the game is a bug. Latency and legibility are the whole brief

decisionRules.if: esports / live scores and stats
decisionRules.then: cyberpunk-neon's own rule bites — it fails on large data tables; keep the dark surface, kill the glow, and let the numbers be the only bright thing

decisionRules.if: the audience is mobile-heavy
decisionRules.then: spatial-3d costs battery, thermals and a 500KB canvas the crawler cannot read — ship a video loop poster instead and keep the WebGL for desktop

decisionRules.if: photosensitivity
decisionRules.then: strobe, glitch and rapid neon flashing is a documented seizure trigger — respect prefers-reduced-motion and put a flashing-lights warning before the trailer, not in the footer

antiPatterns: Key art hidden behind a cookie wall and a newsletter modal
A wall of bullet-point features where three screenshots would do
Neon on neon until the price is unreadable
'Coming soon' with no platform, no date and no wishlist link
A Discord invite as the only support channel

items.name: Streaming / Entertainment
items.pattern: Hero title art with continue-watching over it + rails by category + hover preview + detail sheet + player. The chrome disappears; the artwork is the interface
items.colorMood: Lights down, poster art up — signature red on cinema black where every pixel of chrome gets out of the artwork's way
items.typeMood: Approachable modern consumer — the type never competes with the title treatment on the poster
effects: glass only over the player and the nav — the two places it earns its cost
hover preview after 700ms dwell, muted, never on touch
player chrome fades in 3s and takes the cursor with it
rails scroll by keyboard, not just by mouse drag

decisionRules.if: the surface is a catalog rail or a data table
decisionRules.then: glassmorphism dies — blur destroys the row-scanning edge, and the whole catalog is scanning. Glass belongs on the player overlay and the nav, nowhere else

decisionRules.if: TV / 10-foot interface
decisionRules.then: this is a different product — D-pad focus order, a focus state visible from three metres, 10-foot type, and no hover state exists at all

decisionRules.if: there is no professional key art for every title
decisionRules.then: the whole style collapses — an inconsistent rail of mismatched thumbnails reads as piracy; commission the art or use a uniform typographic tile

decisionRules.if: subtitles/captions
decisionRules.then: they are a product feature not an accessibility checkbox — user-controlled size, background opacity and position, because 80% of usage is not deafness, it is a noisy room

antiPatterns: Autoplay with sound on the browse page
Glass panels over a rail of thumbnails — legibility gone for a screenshot
A 'Continue watching' rail that never forgets the thing you abandoned in episode 1
Hover previews that fire on touch and hijack the tap
Hiding the episode list two clicks deep inside a detail sheet

items.name: Music / Audio
items.pattern: Artist image + latest release + player + tour dates with a buy link per row + discography grid + socials. In-app: now-playing, library, search — nothing else
items.colorMood: Stage-light purple with a hot pink spill — nocturnal and loud, with the album art supplying the actual color
items.typeMood: Loud, flat and undesigned on purpose — type as a blunt instrument, the way a record sleeve does it
effects: album art drives an extracted accent color per track — the mesh takes its hue from the artwork
player chrome as glass over the artwork, the one place it belongs
waveform scrub with a real waveform, not a fake sine
gapless transitions — a 200ms silence between tracks is a product defect

decisionRules.if: artist/release page rather than a streaming product
decisionRules.then: the mesh can go loud and the whole page can be one image — but a tour date row without a buy link is the most common failure in this category, and it costs the actual revenue

decisionRules.if: the surface is a library, queue or search result
decisionRules.then: gradient-mesh and glass both die — a moving color field under a 500-row library is unreadable, and blur kills the scanning edge. Mesh belongs behind the now-playing view only

decisionRules.if: the product is a player people use daily
decisionRules.then: no scroll animation, no reveal, no delight — the delight decays to annoyance by the third session and this is the twentieth session today

decisionRules.if: podcast rather than music
decisionRules.then: different product — chapter marks, speed control, sleep timer and a transcript beat any amount of visual treatment; the artwork matters far less than the resume position

antiPatterns: A player that loses the queue on navigation
Autoplaying the artist's single at full volume on page load
Tour dates as an image
A mesh gradient behind a track listing
Hiding the buy/merch link in a footer while the streaming links get the hero

items.name: News / Editorial
items.pattern: Masthead + lead story at full width + secondary grid + section rails + the article: headline, standfirst, byline, date, body at a 65-character measure, related at the end
items.colorMood: Black on paper with one red for the thing that actually matters — the red is a scarce resource, not a brand color
items.typeMood: A newspaper that moved online without losing its spine — the words are the design
effects: measure locked to 65-75 characters regardless of viewport
reading progress as a hairline, not a percentage badge
images load at their real aspect ratio — a reflowing article is an unreadable article
no scroll-triggered reveals on body text: it hides content from Ctrl+F and from readers

decisionRules.if: the business model is subscription
decisionRules.then: the paywall must appear before the reader invests, not three paragraphs in — the meter that interrupts mid-sentence generates cancellations, not conversions. And never serve the full text to Google while blocking the human who followed the link

decisionRules.if: breaking news / live blog
decisionRules.then: monochrome gives up the channel that says 'updated' — bring one live indicator color back, timestamp every entry, and never silently rewrite a published line

decisionRules.if: the content is CMS-driven with dozens of authors
decisionRules.then: no hand-tuned typographic headlines — a 12vw display line breaks the moment a sub-editor writes a long one. Set a range and test the longest real headline, not the demo one

decisionRules.if: ads fund the site
decisionRules.then: reserve the slot's height in CSS before the ad loads — layout shift under a reader's thumb is the most-complained-about defect in this entire category

antiPatterns: Newsletter modal over the first paragraph
Infinite scroll that loads the next article and steals the URL
Autoplay video that follows you down the page
'Read more' truncation on an article you already opened
A 65-character measure abandoned on desktop so the line runs 140 characters wide

items.name: Portfolio / Creative
items.pattern: Name + one line of what you do + selected work as a grid + case study: problem, approach, outcome, artefacts + about with a real face + a contact that is an email address
items.colorMood: Gallery walls — warm paper and ink, with a burnt-orange hyperlink as the only chroma; the work in the grid is the only loud thing
items.typeMood: International Style discipline — one voice, two optical sizes, nothing decorative anywhere
effects: image reveal on load, never on scroll — the grid is the point and it should be there
hover shows the project name, not a filter or a zoom
cursor stays a cursor
case studies open as pages with real URLs, not as modals

decisionRules.if: the goal is getting hired
decisionRules.then: outcome beats artefact — 'cut onboarding drop-off 34%' with the before/after does more than twelve dribbble shots. Six projects with reasoning beats twenty with mockups, every time

decisionRules.if: this is a design portfolio judged by designers
decisionRules.then: swiss-minimal has no tolerance — one 13px margin in a 16px system breaks the entire illusion and the reviewer will see it before they read a word. If nobody is checking the grid, use a looser style honestly

decisionRules.if: the work is under NDA
decisionRules.then: write the reasoning without the artefact — a portfolio of process, constraints and trade-offs reads as more senior than a wall of pretty screens anyway

decisionRules.if: you are a developer rather than a designer
decisionRules.then: do not attempt this — go typographic or brutalist on purpose; an almost-Swiss grid reads as a failed attempt, while a deliberate plain page reads as confidence

antiPatterns: A 3D WebGL hero that takes 4 seconds and says nothing about the work
Case studies that are a mood board with no problem statement
A contact form instead of an email address
Scroll-jacking between projects
'Passionate about pixel-perfect design' as the opening line

items.name: Agency / Studio
items.pattern: One enormous statement + selected clients + the work as case studies with numbers + services + the team as real people + a brief-shaped contact form
items.colorMood: Near-black with an acid lime that behaves like a highlighter — confident and slightly rude
items.typeMood: A hand-set poster on a landing page — deliberately imperfect, extremely loud, and it had better be on purpose
effects: type assembles once on load — the statement is the product demo
work tiles play a 3-second loop on hover
page transitions carry the acid across the cut
prefers-reduced-motion collapses all of it to a fade and the site still works

decisionRules.if: the site is the portfolio (it is)
decisionRules.then: motion is a demo of the craft you are selling, so it must be flawless — a janky reveal on an agency site is a live demonstration that you cannot do the thing you charge for

decisionRules.if: the buyer is a procurement department at an enterprise
decisionRules.then: acid and swagger stop at the case-study boundary — put the numbers, the timeline and the team in a plain layout, because the person approving the invoice is not the person who liked the animation

decisionRules.if: the client base is regulated (pharma, finance, public sector)
decisionRules.then: drop agency-acid for the pitch surface — it signals 'we will be a governance problem'; keep it for the culture pages

decisionRules.if: the copy is edited by a marketer without a designer
decisionRules.then: typographic breaks — the 12vw statement only works at the length it was set for. Lock the character count or lock the editor out

antiPatterns: 'We are a full-service digital agency' — indistinguishable from 10,000 sites
Case studies with no numbers, only adjectives
A scroll-jacked hero that adds four seconds before the work
Stock team photos on an About page
An awards row above the work itself

items.name: Developer Tools
items.pattern: Hero with the install command copyable + a real code block showing the actual API + 'why this exists' + benchmarks or guarantees + docs link that is more prominent than the sales CTA + pricing with a real free tier
items.colorMood: Slate surfaces, a functional blue, and a green that only ever means passing
items.typeMood: The default voice of a well-built developer product — rational, unfussy, confident enough not to decorate
effects: copy button on every code block, with a copied confirmation
syntax highlighting that matches the reader's editor theme, not your brand
tabs for language/runtime that persist across pages
no scroll animation — this reader opened three tabs and will close two

decisionRules.if: the visitor is an engineer evaluating in under 60 seconds
decisionRules.then: the code block IS the hero — show the actual API, not a diagram of it. A dev tool that explains its value proposition before showing its interface loses to one that pastes ten lines

decisionRules.if: the buyer is a VP or procurement rather than the engineer
decisionRules.then: aurora-glow reads as a genre signal they do not speak, and terminal-cli reads as an error screen — build a separate, plain page for them; do not compromise the developer page to reach them

decisionRules.if: the brand needs to be distinguishable
decisionRules.then: aurora-glow is the problem, not the solution — as of 2026 every dev tool is a dark page with a violet glow. If differentiation matters more than genre-fit, go the other way entirely and ship a white page

decisionRules.if: there is long prose (concepts, guides, rationale)
decisionRules.then: terminal-cli stops at the code block — monospace measurably slows reading, so body text goes to the sans

antiPatterns: A hero that describes the tool without showing it
'Contact sales' as the only path to knowing the price
A docs link buried in the footer
Benchmarks with no methodology, no versions and no repo
Terminal aesthetics on a page aimed at the person signing the cheque

pages.pricing: Free tier that a real project fits in, then usage-based, then enterprise. State the unit and the overage. Engineers will find the trap; do not set one.

items.name: AI / ML Product
items.pattern: Hero with a live demo you can type into + what it does and does not do + how it works + evals/benchmarks with methodology + pricing per token or seat + safety and data-use statement + docs
items.colorMood: Iris violet bleeding into cyan — generative rather than corporate, and the current house style of the category
items.typeMood: Engineered but faintly alien — a research lab that also ships a product and has not decided which it is
effects: streaming tokens render as they arrive — a spinner on an LLM response wastes the one thing you have, which is early output
stop button available the entire time a response is generating
citations render inline as the claim appears, not appended at the end
no fake typing animation on cached content — it is a lie the user will catch

decisionRules.if: the model can be confidently wrong (it can)
decisionRules.then: uncertainty is a first-class UI element — cite the source at the claim, make 'I don't know' a designed state rather than a failure, and never render a hallucination in the same visual voice as a retrieved fact

decisionRules.if: the output feeds a consequential decision (medical, legal, financial, hiring)
decisionRules.then: the human-review step cannot be a checkbox — the UI must make editing easier than accepting, or you have built an automation-bias machine with a disclaimer on it

decisionRules.if: user data trains the model
decisionRules.then: that sentence appears in the UI at the point of input, in plain words, with the opt-out one click away — burying it in a ToS is now a regulatory exposure, not a growth tactic

decisionRules.if: differentiation matters
decisionRules.then: neural-iris + aurora-glow is what every AI product shipped in 2024-2026 — it buys instant category recognition and zero memorability. Choose deliberately which one you need

antiPatterns: A chat box as the entire product with no affordance for what to type
Benchmarks with no methodology, no baseline and no version
A spinner instead of streaming
'Powered by AI' as the value proposition
Confident output with no citation and no uncertainty signal

items.name: Analytics Dashboard
items.pattern: Global filter bar (date, segment) + KPI row with deltas + one primary chart + supporting breakdown table + export. Everything answers 'what changed and why'
items.colorMood: Deep blue-slate that stays readable at 2am, with cyan and amber reserved strictly for series color and thresholds
items.typeMood: Dense, calm instrumentation — the numbers are the design, the type is just the chrome
effects: tabular-nums everywhere so columns of figures align
chart tooltips follow the cursor without occluding the point they describe
loading a chart keeps the axes and skeletons the plot area — no reflow when data lands
no easing on data updates; a bar that animates to a new value hides the jump

decisionRules.if: the user stares at this eight hours a day
decisionRules.then: density is the feature — 18px type and generous whitespace cost the rows they came for. This is the one category where high-contrast-a11y's own advice does not apply, and cramped is correct

decisionRules.if: the background is a gradient, mesh or glass
decisionRules.then: delete it — it corrupts every color you plot on top, and series color is the only encoding a chart has. data-dense and gradient-mesh together is a bug, not a style

decisionRules.if: more than ~6 series on one chart
decisionRules.then: you have run out of distinguishable colors before your users have run out of color-vision deficiencies — switch to small multiples, direct labels, or let the user pick the series

decisionRules.if: the dashboard will be viewed on mobile
decisionRules.then: it is a different product — a KPI list and one sparkline; the table does not survive, and pretending it does produces a horizontal scroll nobody uses

antiPatterns: A wall of 20 KPI tiles where none is the answer to anything
Red/green as the only up/down signal
Charts with no baseline, no comparison and no units
A 3D pie chart
Dark mode as the only mode — this gets projected in meetings and printed for boards

pages.dashboard: Global filters pinned top, KPI row with deltas and comparison period, one primary chart, one breakdown table. Density over whitespace. Every tile states its unit and its time window.

items.name: Productivity / Notes
items.pattern: Hero showing the actual app + one keyboard shortcut as the proof + templates + sync/offline claim + pricing + a real free tier. In-app: content first, chrome on demand
items.colorMood: A desk with nothing on it — warm graphite and paper, with a single amber for the one thing due today
items.typeMood: One voice, two optical sizes, nothing decorative anywhere — the user's words must be the most interesting thing on screen
effects: every action has a keyboard path and the UI teaches it in the tooltip
autosave with a stated timestamp, never a Save button that can be forgotten
chrome fades while typing and returns on mouse move
no animation on list reorder beyond 120ms — this is a daily action

decisionRules.if: the user opens this 40 times a day
decisionRules.then: every millisecond of animation is paid 40 times — cut all of it. The delight decays to annoyance by the third visit and this is the four-hundredth

decisionRules.if: the product competes on focus
decisionRules.then: the design argument is subtraction — a focus tool with a sidebar, a toolbar, a right rail and an AI button has already lost the argument it is making

decisionRules.if: content is user-generated and long
decisionRules.then: swiss-minimal's whitespace budget goes to the measure, not the chrome — 65-75 characters, and the note list must survive 5,000 notes without a redesign

decisionRules.if: offline is claimed
decisionRules.then: the conflict-resolution UI is the actual product — two devices, one note, no network is the case that decides whether people trust you with their thinking

antiPatterns: An onboarding tour of 11 steps before the user can write a word
A 'quick capture' that takes four taps
Amber spent on decoration so it no longer means 'due today'
AI features that write over the cursor without being asked
Templates as the hero when the empty note is the product

items.name: Social / Community
items.pattern: Feed as the whole product + composer always reachable + profile + notifications + search. Everything else is a settings page nobody visits
items.colorMood: Fuchsia with a tangerine — a sunset pulled apart into two usable tokens, warm and a little hot
items.typeMood: Approachable modern consumer — the type gets out of the way of user content, which supplies all the real color
effects: optimistic UI on every interaction — a like that waits for the server feels broken
new-posts pill rather than auto-injecting content above the reader's scroll position
illustration only in empty states and errors, never in the feed
no infinite-scroll on a profile — people came to find one thing

decisionRules.if: the feed is ranked rather than chronological
decisionRules.then: say so in the UI and offer the chronological switch — the single largest trust complaint in this category is not the ranking, it is discovering the ranking existed

decisionRules.if: the product has any moderation surface
decisionRules.then: design the block/report/mute path before the composer — a community product ships its harassment tooling at launch or it ships its harassment problem at launch

decisionRules.if: engagement metrics are visible
decisionRules.then: decide whose interest they serve — public follower counts and read receipts are design decisions with documented mental-health outcomes for teenage users; 'everyone does it' is not the rationale you want in the deposition

decisionRules.if: the feed carries user photography and video
decisionRules.then: reserve the aspect ratio before load — content that shifts under a scrolling thumb causes mis-taps on Report and Follow alike

antiPatterns: Infinite scroll with no end state and no time-spent signal
Notification badges for engagement that is not about the user
A composer that loses a long draft on navigation
Dark patterns in the deactivate flow
Illustration in the feed competing with the users' own images

items.name: Travel / Booking
items.pattern: Full-bleed destination image + search widget over it (the actual product) + results with real prices + property/flight detail + transparent total + booking. The image sells, the search converts
items.colorMood: Window seat at altitude — sky blue over sand with a coral reserved for fares and deals
items.typeMood: Somewhere old and worth the flight — inscriptional capitals over air and horizon
effects: search widget is above the fold and focused on load — it is the product, not a decoration on the hero
price changes announce themselves rather than silently updating
map and list stay in sync, both scrollable
images are the actual property, dated, never a stock beach

decisionRules.if: a price is displayed
decisionRules.then: it is the total the user will pay including taxes and mandatory fees — drip pricing is now enforcement territory in the EU, UK and US simultaneously, and it is also the top-rated reason people abandon this category

decisionRules.if: the traveller is mid-trip rather than dreaming
decisionRules.then: the whole design inverts — they are on roaming data, one bar, in a taxi. Booking reference, address in the local language, and the phone number, offline and above everything else. Photography is dead weight here

decisionRules.if: there is no professional photography of the actual property
decisionRules.then: photographic collapses into a trust problem — a stock hero next to a real listing photo reads as bait-and-switch. Show the real room even if it is worse

decisionRules.if: gradient-mesh sits behind body text or a results list
decisionRules.then: kill it — it belongs behind the search widget and nowhere else; a moving color field under a fare table is unreadable

antiPatterns: 'From £29' where £29 has never existed on any date
Scarcity timers on a hotel with 40 rooms free
A 2MB hero that delays the search widget people came for
Booking confirmation that is not emailed and not saved offline
Cookie wall before the destination is even visible

pages.search-results: Filters in a left rail persisting in the URL, map synced on the right, total price per row, sort visible and honest. Result count stated.

items.name: Real Estate / Property
items.pattern: Search or featured property + listing grid with price, beds, area + property page: gallery, key facts, floor plan, map, neighbourhood, agent + arrange-viewing CTA
items.colorMood: Sage green, limestone and brass — old money without the crest; a considered purchase, not a lead form
items.typeMood: Inscriptional and architectural — the building is the hero and the type behaves like a plaque next to it
effects: gallery is the interface — full-bleed, keyboard navigable, with the floor plan in the same reel
key facts (price, beds, baths, m²) never scroll away on desktop
map lazy-loads on intent, not on page load
no hover zoom on a photo of a room — it reads as a stock library

decisionRules.if: the visitor is buying rather than browsing
decisionRules.then: price, area, floor plan and location are the whole decision — a property page without a floor plan and an m² figure is optimising the wrong thing, however good the photography is

decisionRules.if: the listing is rental at volume
decisionRules.then: editorial-magazine collapses — it is half imagery by weight and it assumes long content. Rentals are a table with photos; use the listing grid honestly and spend the design on the filters

decisionRules.if: the product is lead-gen for agents
decisionRules.then: be honest about it — a 'contact agent' form that gates the address turns a buyer into a lead and a brand into a spam sender. The address is not the moat

decisionRules.if: photography is agent-supplied and inconsistent
decisionRules.then: photographic is not available to you — normalise with a uniform tile, a required aspect ratio and a floor-plan-first layout, or the grid reads as a scam listing next to a professional one

antiPatterns: Wide-angle lens distortion that makes a 9m² box look like a loft
'Price on application' on a residential listing
A virtual tour that requires a plugin and 30 seconds
Photos with no room labels and no floor plan to place them in
Gating the address behind a registration wall

items.name: Automotive / Hardware
items.pattern: Hero of the object rotating or full-bleed + spec strip + configurator + gallery + technology sections + finance/price + book a test drive or buy
items.colorMood: Machined gunmetal with a brake-light red — engineered and cold to the touch; the red is a warning, not a brand flourish
items.typeMood: HUD energy — clipped corners and angular terminals, the way an instrument cluster labels things
effects: configurator updates the render and the price in the same frame — a lag between them breaks the causal link
colour swatches are rendered on the actual car, never a hex circle
3D falls back to a pre-rendered turntable video below a device threshold
spec numbers in tabular figures so trims compare vertically

decisionRules.if: the audience is mobile-heavy
decisionRules.then: spatial-3d is a thermal and battery cost they pay for your art direction — ship a turntable video, keep the WebGL behind a desktop check, and never make the canvas the only path to the spec

decisionRules.if: the 3D content needs to be found in search
decisionRules.then: a canvas does not exist to a crawler — every configuration, spec and trim needs a real URL with real text, or the most expensive part of the site is invisible to the people looking for it

decisionRules.if: the screen is in-vehicle (IVI/HMI)
decisionRules.then: entirely different rules — glance time under 2 seconds, targets sized for a moving car, no dark-luxury hairlines, and nothing that requires reading a sentence. This is a safety surface with a regulator attached

decisionRules.if: the product is a configurator with a real price
decisionRules.then: the running total is visible at all times and every option states its cost — a price that only resolves at the summary screen is the abandonment point in every funnel in this category

antiPatterns: A WebGL hero that takes 6 seconds before a single spec is visible
Colour swatches as flat hex circles next to a photorealistic render
Spec sheets as a downloadable PDF
'From $X' where X is a trim that cannot be ordered
Dark-luxury gold hairlines on a parts catalog of 400 SKUs

items.name: Legal / Law Firm
items.pattern: Firm name + practice areas + the people with real credentials + notable matters + insights/publications + offices + a contact that reaches a human
items.colorMood: Oxblood on cream with brass — leather-bound and unbothered, because blue would read as a tech startup
items.typeMood: Scholarly and unshowy — the argument matters and the typography gets out of its way
effects: no motion anywhere — gravitas is the product and movement spends it
people photographed against a real wall, not a gradient
publications as readable pages with dates, not gated PDFs
hairline rules to separate, never cards with shadows

decisionRules.if: the visitor is a distressed individual (injury, family, immigration, criminal)
decisionRules.then: this is not a corporate brochure — plain language at grade-8, the phone number in the header, 'what happens next' before 'about our firm', and no jargon between them and help. The oxblood gravitas serves the firm; the clarity serves the client, and the client is the one converting

decisionRules.if: the client base is corporate/M&A
decisionRules.then: credentials are the design — named partners, real matters, real jurisdictions. A stock gavel photograph actively costs credibility with this buyer

decisionRules.if: any statement could be construed as legal advice
decisionRules.then: the disclaimer renders at body size at the point of the claim, not in 11px grey in the footer — and never inside a tooltip. The tooltip is not a disclosure and it will not survive scrutiny

decisionRules.if: the site is CMS-driven with lawyers publishing
decisionRules.then: editorial-magazine breaks on a 200-word post — set a minimum length for that template or it will look abandoned within a month

antiPatterns: Stock photography of a gavel, scales, or a leather-bound library nobody works in
'Free consultation' that is a lead form to a call centre
Attorney bios with no bar admission, no jurisdiction and no matters
A chatbot as the first contact for someone describing an arrest
Neo-brutalism, claymorphism or any toy vocabulary — it quietly undercuts the one thing being sold

items.name: Nonprofit / Charity
items.pattern: One photograph of the actual work + one sentence of the problem + donate CTA (present from the first screen) + what your money does, specifically + impact with real numbers + who we are + financial transparency
items.colorMood: A living green with a coral for urgency — hopeful and human, neither a bank nor a guilt trip
items.typeMood: Plain-spoken and grounded — a report from the field, not a brand campaign
effects: donation amounts as preset buttons with what each one buys, stated
no motion on imagery of people in distress — dignity is a design constraint
impact numbers cite their source and their year
the donate path never leaves the brand

decisionRules.if: donation is the conversion
decisionRules.then: amount buttons must state what they buy ('£25 = a month of clean water for one family') — an empty amount field converts at a fraction of the rate, because the donor does not know what is useful

decisionRules.if: the imagery shows beneficiaries
decisionRules.then: consent, dignity and agency are design decisions — the poverty-porn hero raises money this quarter and costs the organisation its standing permanently. Show people doing, not people suffering

decisionRules.if: the organisation handles emergencies
decisionRules.then: organic-earthy cannot signal urgency — its own rule is that the palette has no danger step. Bring the coral in as a genuine alert token for the appeal surface only, or the crisis banner reads as decoration

decisionRules.if: donors are recurring
decisionRules.then: cancellation must be as easy as signing up — the dark-pattern retention flow is the reputational risk that outlives the retained pound, and in this sector it becomes a news story

antiPatterns: Poverty porn — a child's face as the hero with no name and no consent
'Every donation helps' with no figure showing what any of them do
Financials as a 60-page PDF and no summary
A donate flow that hands off to a third-party page with different branding
Guilt-based interstitials before the visitor has read the problem

items.name: Government / Civic
items.pattern: Search + the top 5 tasks people actually come for + start-a-service + plain-language guide pages + contact including a phone number and an in-person option
items.colorMood: Federal navy, generous neutrals, no decoration — built to survive a screen reader, a five-year-old laptop and a lawsuit
items.typeMood: Designed so the reader never has to work — legibility as the actual brief, not a checkbox
effects: one question per page — the pattern that beat every alternative in real service testing
back button always works, and the browser's back button works too
no JavaScript required for any core task
error summary at the top of the form, linked to each field, announced to assistive tech

decisionRules.if: the user has no alternative supplier (they do not — this is government)
decisionRules.then: every accessibility decision is a legal obligation, not a preference; and the person on a 5-year-old Android on 3G in a library is not an edge case, they are disproportionately the person who needs the service most

decisionRules.if: the service involves money, eligibility or a deadline
decisionRules.then: plain language at grade-8 or below, the eligibility criteria before the form, and 'what happens next' with a real timeframe — the cost of ambiguity here is a phone call to a call centre you are paying for

decisionRules.if: a designer proposes glassmorphism, neumorphism, or any low-contrast aesthetic
decisionRules.then: it is disqualified by rule, not by taste — these styles' own documentation excludes government, and the WCAG floor is statutory (Section 508 / EN 301 549 / EAA)

decisionRules.if: the content is a service rather than information
decisionRules.then: swiss-minimal's whitespace stops at the form — one question per page, 18px floor, and never a two-column form; the grid serves the guide pages, the service needs a queue

antiPatterns: A homepage carousel of the mayor's initiatives above the tax deadline everyone came for
PDFs as the delivery mechanism for a service
Departmental org structure as the navigation
A chatbot in front of a phone number
Any style that trades contrast for aesthetic distinction — it is not yours to trade here

pages.onboarding: One question per page. State why each field is needed and who sees it. Save and return by default — these forms are filled in across days, from libraries.

items.name: Logistics / Fleet
items.pattern: Track-a-shipment first + fleet/inventory overview + exceptions needing action + route or map + reporting. The whole product answers 'where is it and what is broken'
items.colorMood: Hi-vis on steel — warehouse amber against industrial grey, with a green that only ever means delivered
items.typeMood: Dense, calm instrumentation — the numbers are the design, and they get read across a warehouse
effects: exceptions sort to the top by default — the ops user is here for what is broken
status changes announce to screen readers and to the row's aria-live region
no motion on a live map beyond the marker itself
timestamps always with timezone — a fleet crosses them

decisionRules.if: the user is on a shop floor or in a yard
decisionRules.then: 56px targets and maximum contrast — gloves, glare, cold hands and a scanner in the other hand are the design constraint, not the aesthetic. This is why high-contrast sits next to data-dense here despite the tension

decisionRules.if: the user is a driver
decisionRules.then: it is a glance-and-go product — one instruction per screen, offline-first, and never a flow that requires reading a paragraph while the engine is running. A dispatcher's dense table on a driver's phone is a safety defect

decisionRules.if: amber is the brand color
decisionRules.then: it cannot also be the warning color — pick one. A hi-vis palette that uses its alert token for the logo has no way left to say 'delayed'

decisionRules.if: the console runs on a wall display in a depot
decisionRules.then: different product again — read at 4 metres, no interaction, no hover, and the only thing on it is the exception count

antiPatterns: Tracking that requires an account
'Out for delivery' with no time window and no map
Exceptions buried in a tab behind the happy path
A dense dispatcher table shipped unchanged to the driver's phone
Amber used decoratively until it stops meaning anything

pages.dashboard: Exceptions first, then in-transit counts, then the map. Density over whitespace. Every row is actionable or it should not be a row.

items.name: HR / People
items.pattern: Employee home with the 3 things they came for (book leave, payslip, who's out) + manager approvals + admin console + directory. Two user classes, two designs
items.colorMood: Warm plum with a teal that keeps it professional — softer than corporate blue, which matters when the screen is about someone's salary
items.typeMood: Clean geometric modernism — friendly enough to book a holiday in, plain enough to read a payslip in
effects: approval actions are two-step and reversible — an accidental leave rejection is a human conversation
illustration in empty states and onboarding only, never near a salary figure
payslip and contract render as documents, not as cards
dates always with the weekday — 'Fri 12 Sep', because leave is planned in weekdays

decisionRules.if: the screen shows salary, performance, or termination
decisionRules.then: no illustration, no mascot, no plum warmth — a character next to a redundancy notice is the single most-reported design failure in this category. Switch to a plain, document-like surface

decisionRules.if: the user is an employee rather than an HR admin
decisionRules.then: they visit four times a year and they want one thing — do not ship them the admin console's information architecture. Book leave, view payslip, find a colleague. That is the whole product to 95% of the seats

decisionRules.if: recruiting / ATS
decisionRules.then: the candidate is a user with no account, no training and no obligation — a 40-field application form is why your funnel is broken, and rejection emails are a design surface you are currently ignoring

decisionRules.if: the org adopts only half of Material
decisionRules.then: do not adopt it at all — partial Material reads as broken Material, and this is a category where 'broken' reads as 'my payroll data is unsafe'

antiPatterns: A confetti animation on 'Your leave was approved' next to one on 'Your role is at risk'
Cheerful illustration on a payslip
An employee handbook as a 90-page PDF
Performance review UI that makes the rating easier than the comment
Making an employee learn the HR admin's mental model to find their own contract

items.name: Marketplace
items.pattern: Search + category entry + listing grid with photo, price, seller rating + listing page with seller trust + message/buy + separate seller dashboard. Two products in one skin
items.colorMood: Deep teal for the platform, tangerine for the transaction — the color tells you whose surface you are on
items.typeMood: Plain and fast — the seller's photograph and the price are the design; the type just gets out of the way
effects: seller-supplied photos normalised to one aspect ratio with letterboxing, never cropped through the item
price and shipping resolve on the tile, not on the listing page
saved searches notify — the returning buyer is the whole retention model
message thread keeps the listing pinned in context

decisionRules.if: the marketplace is genuinely two-sided
decisionRules.then: buyer and seller surfaces must be visually distinguishable — teal for browse, tangerine for transact. A seller who cannot tell whether they are looking at their listing or a buyer's view will mis-price, and will blame you

decisionRules.if: trust is the actual product (it is)
decisionRules.then: the seller's rating, join date, response rate and dispute path are load-bearing UI, not a badge — a beautiful listing grid on top of an unverifiable seller is a fraud funnel with good typography

decisionRules.if: listings are long lists of like items
decisionRules.then: no bento-grid — a grid of unequal cards promises the reader they can look in any order, which is false for a ranked result set. It is a list; design a list

decisionRules.if: photography is seller-supplied
decisionRules.then: photographic style is not available in its pure form — it assumes art direction you do not control. Enforce a minimum resolution and a uniform tile, or the grid will look like a scam next to any professional listing

antiPatterns: Shipping cost revealed only after the buyer commits
A seller dashboard that is the buyer UI with extra tabs
Ratings with no volume — '5.0' from one review shown as five stars
Contact-seller gated behind an account before the price is visible
A 'featured' rail that is indistinguishable from organic results

items.name: Dating / Relationships
items.pattern: Photo-first profile card + a decision + a match + a conversation. Everything else is settings. The product is one screen repeated
items.colorMood: Rose and peach with a violet undertow — flushed but not tacky, warmth without a heart-shaped cursor
items.typeMood: Approachable modern consumer — the profile photo is the design, the type is the caption
effects: photos at a real aspect ratio, never cropped through a face
the block and report action is reachable from every surface a person appears on
no read receipts by default — asymmetric anxiety is a design decision
mesh behind the empty state and the match moment only

decisionRules.if: the product connects strangers in physical space (it does)
decisionRules.then: safety is the primary design surface, not a settings sub-page — block, report, photo verification, location fuzzing and a share-my-date path ship at launch or the product ships a harm at launch

decisionRules.if: monetisation is engagement-based
decisionRules.then: you have designed a conflict of interest into the product — a successful match is a churned user. Decide it consciously, because the dark patterns in this category (paywalled likes, artificial scarcity, ghost profiles) are now regulatory and journalistic targets

decisionRules.if: the surface is a conversation or a profile detail
decisionRules.then: gradient-mesh dies — a moving color field under a stranger's bio is unreadable, and this is the text that decides whether someone feels safe meeting them

decisionRules.if: the user base includes LGBTQ+ users in hostile jurisdictions
decisionRules.then: the design carries a threat model — no exact distance, no outing through a notification, discreet-mode as a first-class feature. This is not an edge case; it is a documented arrest vector

antiPatterns: Paywalling the ability to see who liked you
Distance displayed precisely enough to triangulate
A report flow that takes more taps than a like
Fake profiles or 'someone liked you' notifications with nobody behind them
Read receipts on by default

items.name: Sports / Live Scores
items.pattern: Live scores strip pinned + today's fixtures + the match centre (score, timeline, lineups, stats) + standings table + team pages. Speed and the number, nothing else
items.colorMood: Scarlet on midnight with a floodlight yellow — built for big numbers read from the back of the room
items.typeMood: Stadium volume — ultra-condensed caps hitting like a scoreboard; the score is always the largest thing on the screen
effects: score updates push without a refresh and without moving anything else on the page
a goal announces via aria-live — blind fans follow live scores too
tabular-nums on every score, time and table position
no celebration animation over a live score — someone is checking it in a meeting

decisionRules.if: the user is checking a live score
decisionRules.then: they gave you 2 seconds and one glance — the score is the page. Anything above it (a cookie banner, an interstitial, a 'download our app' rail) is the design failing at its only job

decisionRules.if: the product covers a sport with a betting market
decisionRules.then: the odds surface must be visually separable from the editorial surface, with the regulator's disclosure at body size — and never in a tooltip. This is enforcement territory in the UK, EU and US alike

decisionRules.if: match centre / stats
decisionRules.then: density is right and high-contrast-a11y's 18px advice does not apply to the stats table — but it absolutely applies to the score itself, which is read at arm's length in a pub

decisionRules.if: a fan is on a stadium wifi that does not work
decisionRules.then: the score must render server-side and the page must survive a dead socket — a live product that shows a spinner during the goal is the one moment it had to work

antiPatterns: An interstitial ad over a live score
Scores that only update on a manual refresh
A standings table that scrolls horizontally on mobile
Autoplaying highlight video that spoils the score above it
Scarlet on midnight at 3:1 for the actual score

items.name: Photography
items.pattern: One image, full-bleed, no chrome + series index + the series as a sequence + about + prints or enquiries. Navigation is a word in a corner
items.colorMood: Safelight — neutral greys calibrated not to lie about a photograph, with amber as the only chroma in the chrome
items.typeMood: Art direction confidence — extreme contrast in the type so the photograph never has to compete with it
effects: images at full quality with a progressive load — a photographer's site that ships a compressed JPEG has already failed
cross-fade between frames, 400ms, no slide
keyboard arrows navigate the series
zero UI over the image — the caption lives below it

decisionRules.if: the work is colour photography
decisionRules.then: the chrome must be neutral grey and nothing else — any brand hue in the frame shifts the perceived colour of the work. This is the entire reason darkroom-amber is calibrated the way it is, and why monochrome is the right style rather than a stylistic preference

decisionRules.if: the site sells prints
decisionRules.then: it becomes an e-commerce product wearing a gallery's clothes — size, paper, edition and shipping are the decision, and monochrome gives up the channel that says 'out of stock'. Bring a real status color into the shop path only

decisionRules.if: the audience is art directors hiring
decisionRules.then: twelve images beat two hundred — and the series must be sequenced, because sequencing is the skill being assessed. A masonry wall of everything says you cannot edit

decisionRules.if: image theft is a concern
decisionRules.then: right-click blockers do not work and read as amateur — watermark deliberately or accept it; the design decision is which, not whether to fight the browser

antiPatterns: A splash page with an 'Enter' link
Right-click disabled
Masonry grid of 200 unedited frames
Music on load
Any brand color inside the frame of a colour photograph

items.name: Minimal / Personal Site
items.pattern: Name + one line of who you are + what you are doing now + writing + links. One page, no nav, no hero
items.colorMood: Nothing but greys and one blue that only appears when you can click it — the content has to carry the design
items.typeMood: Composed and literate — high-contrast elegance that still behaves itself on an about page
effects: no animation at all — a personal site that fades in reads as a template
links underlined, because that is what a link is
the whole page is one request
dark mode from prefers-color-scheme, with no toggle to build

decisionRules.if: you are not going to maintain it (you are not)
decisionRules.then: one static page beats a blog with three posts from 2023 — a 'Latest writing' section with a stale date actively costs credibility. Ship the page, not the CMS

decisionRules.if: the site exists to get you hired or known
decisionRules.then: 'what I am doing now' and 'what I have made' are the only two sections that do work — an about page of adjectives converts nobody

decisionRules.if: there is real writing here
decisionRules.then: the measure is the whole design — 65-75 characters, 1.6 line height, and a serif is a legitimate choice for the body. Everything else is decoration you will regret

decisionRules.if: you want personality rather than restraint
decisionRules.then: do not use swiss-minimal — it hides personality by construction, and a personal site whose only asset is personality is the exact case its own documentation excludes. Go brutalist or illustrated and mean it

antiPatterns: A splash animation of your own name
A blog with two posts and a 'Read more' link to nothing
Skill bars claiming 87% CSS
A contact form on a personal site instead of an email address
Reinventing the underline as a 1px hover animation nobody recognises as a link

items.name: Brutalist / Experimental
items.pattern: There is no pattern — that is the point. But: the thing itself, immediately, with no preamble; navigation as raw text; and an exit to something real
items.colorMood: Raw concrete, hard black rules and a warning yellow — unfinished on purpose, and the 'on purpose' is the entire load-bearing claim
items.typeMood: Loud, flat and undesigned on purpose — type as a blunt instrument
effects: default browser focus rings, kept deliberately
system fonts where it serves the joke
no transitions — state changes are instant and jarring by design
the page weighs 30KB and that is part of the argument

decisionRules.if: the audience did not opt into the joke
decisionRules.then: brutalism reads as broken, not as intentional — this style requires a reader who recognises the reference. Outside that audience you have not made a statement, you have made a bug report

decisionRules.if: there is a checkout, a signup, or anything asking for trust
decisionRules.then: the raw aesthetic stops at that boundary — friction reads as broken and kills conversion, and 'products asking to be trusted with money or health data' is this style's own explicit exclusion

decisionRules.if: accessibility
decisionRules.then: brutalism is not an excuse — default focus rings and semantic HTML are actually easier here than in a designed system. A brutalist site failing WCAG is just a badly built site with a good story

decisionRules.if: the client is paying for this
decisionRules.then: get the reference agreed in writing before you build — this is the style most likely to be received as 'unfinished' by the one stakeholder who was not in the kickoff

antiPatterns: Brutalism as an excuse for an unusable navigation
Comic Sans as the entire idea
A manifesto with no work behind it
Copying a 2018 brutalist template — the whole premise was not doing that
Anti-design that took three weeks and looks like it took three weeks

items.name: Terminal / CLI Tool
items.pattern: The install command, copyable, first + an asciinema of the tool doing the thing + flags/usage + why it beats the alternative + a link to the repo. Under 800px tall
items.colorMood: A CRT that never got switched off — phosphor green on near-black, with amber for warnings and nothing else
items.typeMood: Everything is monospaced and that is the entire aesthetic
effects: asciinema/SVG cast rather than a video — it is text, it should stay text and stay copyable
install command has a copy button and shows the checksum
no scroll animation; the reader is in a terminal in the next window
the page works with JS off

decisionRules.if: there is prose (concepts, guides, rationale)
decisionRules.then: monospace stops at the code block — it measurably slows reading, so the explanation goes to a sans and only the commands stay in the character grid

decisionRules.if: the page is aimed at a buyer rather than a user
decisionRules.then: terminal-cli reads as an error screen to a non-technical audience — build them a different page entirely rather than diluting this one

decisionRules.if: mobile traffic matters
decisionRules.then: a character grid does not reflow — accept that this page is a desktop artefact, keep the install command as the one thing that works at 375px, and do not try to make an 80-column TUI responsive

decisionRules.if: the install is 'curl | sh'
decisionRules.then: show the script's URL and the checksum next to it — a piped shell script asking for blind trust is the one design decision this audience will actually publicly criticise

antiPatterns: A green-on-black marketing site for a tool that is not a terminal tool
A video of a terminal instead of copyable text
'npm install' with no mention of the actual size or dependency count
A landing page taller than the tool's own README
Fake typing animations in the demo

items.name: Documentation Site
items.pattern: Search (the real navigation) + three-column: nav rail, content at a fixed measure, on-this-page rail + quickstart before concepts + copyable examples throughout + versioned
items.colorMood: Greys and one blue that only appears when you can click it — the safest possible base when the content must carry everything
items.typeMood: Headlines set in code, prose set in a sans — for a reader who has three tabs open and 40 seconds
effects: search is keyboard-first (Cmd+K) and it is the primary navigation, not the sidebar
every code block is copyable and language-tabbed, with the tab persisting across pages
