anchor links on every heading, because this page will be linked from a Slack thread
no scroll-triggered anything — Ctrl+F must find everything on the page

decisionRules.if: the reader arrived from Google with an error message
decisionRules.then: they are not reading your guide — they are Ctrl+F-ing for a string. Scroll-reveal, tabs that hide content, and accordions all hide text from Ctrl+F and from the crawler that sent them. Nothing may be collapsed by default

decisionRules.if: the product is versioned
decisionRules.then: the version selector is in the header and the URL, and the page states which version it is — docs that silently show latest to someone on v2 generate the support load the docs existed to prevent

decisionRules.if: there are conceptual guides and API reference
decisionRules.then: they are different products in one skin — the guide is prose at a 70-character measure, the reference is a table. Do not set the reference in prose or the guide in a table

decisionRules.if: design distinction is being proposed
decisionRules.then: resist it — docs are the one category where being identical to every other docs site is a feature. The reader's muscle memory is worth more than your brand expression

antiPatterns: Search that only matches page titles
A quickstart that requires reading the concepts first
Code examples that are not runnable and not copyable
Content behind tabs and accordions where Ctrl+F cannot reach it
No indication of which version you are reading

items.name: Sustainable / Artisan Brand
items.pattern: One photograph of the material or the hands making it + the claim + how it is made + provenance and materials + the products + the impact numbers with a source + shop
items.colorMood: Clay, moss and oat — pigments that look mixed rather than picked; nothing in the palette can shout, and that is the point
items.typeMood: An old soul with a modern printing press — warm, slightly strange, and built for people who actually read the provenance
effects: photography of process and material, not of a product on white
no motion — slow is the brand claim and a parallax contradicts it
provenance stated inline as a fact, not as a badge
texture from warm tone shifts, never from a noise overlay

decisionRules.if: a sustainability claim is made
decisionRules.then: it needs a number, a scope and a source at the point of the claim — 'eco-friendly' with no methodology is greenwashing, and it is now actively enforced (EU Green Claims, CMA, FTC). The design decision is where the evidence renders, not whether to include it

decisionRules.if: this is also a shop
decisionRules.then: organic-earthy cannot signal 'out of stock', 'payment failed' or 'order delayed' — its own rule is that muted pigments give you no contrast steps for urgency. Bring one real alert token into the commerce path only

decisionRules.if: the products are genuinely handmade
decisionRules.then: variation is the selling point, so photograph the variation — a uniform grid of identical shots contradicts the entire claim and reads as drop-shipped

decisionRules.if: the brand is a large company with a sustainable line
decisionRules.then: earthy pigments on a mass-market product is the visual grammar of greenwashing and the audience reads it instantly — earn it with the supply chain page or do not reach for the clay

antiPatterns: A green leaf icon as the entire sustainability story
'Eco-friendly' with no number, no scope and no source
Kraft-paper texture as a substitute for an actual supply chain
Products shot on white in a brand built on material and process
Carbon-offset badges linking to nothing

items.name: Accessibility-First Product
items.pattern: Plain hero, one claim + the task, immediately + linear content at a real measure + forms one question at a time + a genuine accessibility statement with a contact and a known-issues list
items.colorMood: Every pair pushed well past AA and most of the way to AAA — for when low vision, sunlight or a legal floor is the actual constraint
items.typeMood: Designed so the reader never has to work — Atkinson Hyperlegible exists because letterform confusion is the failure mode, not font size
effects: focus visible at 3:1 against both the component and the page, and never removed
prefers-reduced-motion honoured by removing the motion, not by shortening it
every state announced in text as well as color
the product works at 200% zoom and at 320px without horizontal scroll

decisionRules.if: accessibility is being treated as a checklist to tick once
decisionRules.then: stop — high-contrast-a11y is the floor under every other style in this database, not a box. A product that is 'the accessible one' while the rest of the range is not has described its own problem

decisionRules.if: the user is an expert using this daily (a screen-reader power user)
decisionRules.then: 18px type and huge targets cost them rows and speed — they navigate by landmark and heading at 400 words per minute. Correct semantics beat big type for this user, and the two are constantly confused

decisionRules.if: an automated audit passes
decisionRules.then: you have cleared roughly 30% of the criteria — focus order, error recovery, and whether a task is completable by keyboard are not machine-detectable. Test with a real screen reader or the badge is decoration

decisionRules.if: the brand wants aesthetic distinction
decisionRules.then: this style spends its budget elsewhere on purpose — that is the trade. Spend the distinction on voice, layout and content instead of on contrast, which is not yours to trade

antiPatterns: An overlay widget that claims one-line compliance — they are demonstrably harmful and they are the leading cause of lawsuits, not the cure
Removing focus outlines because they are ugly
An accessibility statement with no contact, no date and no known issues
'Skip to content' that does not move focus
Color as the only carrier of an error, a status, or a required field
